0.headline: Purple Style Labs IPO booked 28% so far on last day; retail portion fully subscribed
0.heading: Purple Style Labs IPO booked 28% so far on last day; retail portion fully subscribed
0.intro: Purple Style Labs, the parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, continued to see muted investor interest on the final day of its initial public offering (IPO), with the issue subscribed 28 percent as of 11:20 am on September 2, according to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
0.body:
Purple Style Labs, the parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, continued to see muted investor interest on the final day of its initial public offering (IPO), with the issue subscribed 28 percent as of 11:20 am on September 2, according to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Rs 680-crore IPO received bids for 19,51,872 equity shares against 68,49,816 shares on offer. Retail investors led the subscription with 1.16 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 16 percent.

The IPO has a price band of Rs 546 to Rs 575 per share and will remain open for subscription until September 2. The issue comprises entirely a fresh issue of equity shares.

Read Also: Rays of Belief IPO subscribed over 1.5x so far on Day 2; retail portion booked 8x

In the grey market, Purple Style Labs shares were commanding a premium of Rs 1 per share on the morning of September 2, according to InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 575, this translates into an indicative listing price of Rs 576 and a potential gain of nearly 0.26 percent.

GMP figures are unofficial and are based on activity in the unregulated grey market. They can change before listing and should not be treated as a guarantee of the actual listing price or returns.

Ahead of the public issue, Purple Style Labs raised Rs 306 crore from anchor investors on August 28. The company allotted about 53.22 lakh equity shares at Rs 575 apiece to 10 anchor investors, according to exchange filings.

The anchor book included names such as Morgan Stanley Asia, BofA Securities Europe, Integrated Core Strategies, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Jupiter India Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, ITI Mutual Fund and Singularity Equity Fund I.

Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 371.1 crore is proposed to be invested in subsidiary PSL Retail for expenditure related to lease liabilities for Experience Centers and back-end offices in India. Another Rs 138.9 crore is earmarked for sales and marketing expenditure, with the balance intended for general corporate purposes.

Purple Style Labs reported revenue from operations of about Rs 557.8 crore in FY26, up from Rs 489.9 crore in FY25. However, its net loss widened to about Rs 285.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 188.3 crore in the previous fiscal.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers for the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

The shares are scheduled to be listed on the BSE and NSE on September 7.

Check IPO News Here

About Purple Style Labs

Purple Style Labs operates Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, an omnichannel luxury fashion platform offering designer products across women’s wear, men’s wear and other categories, with a focus on wedding and occasion wear.

The company sources products from a large network of designer brands and operates 14 Experience Centers, including 12 in metropolitan cities in India, alongside its online channels, events and exhibitions.

1.headline: Deepa Jewellers IPO fully subscribed on second day of bidding; GMP at 25%
1.heading: Deepa Jewellers IPO fully subscribed on second day of bidding; GMP at 25%
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of the Telangana-based hallmarked gold jewellery supplier, Deepa Jewellers, witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 1.3 times subscription as of 10:30 am on September 2, as per the NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of the Telangana-based hallmarked gold jewellery supplier, Deepa Jewellers, witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 1.3 times subscription as of 10:30 am on September 2, as per the NSE data.

The IPO received bids for 2,40,57,516 equity shares against 1,85,20,085 shares on offer, with retail investors accounting for 2.01 times subscription of their reserved portion. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 1.17 times during the period.

The Telangana-based company, which supplies hallmarked gold jewellery to retail chains and standalone stores, has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 168-177 per share. The issue will remain open until September 3.

Read Also: ESDS Software IPO allotment today: Check status on BSE, NSE and registrar; GMP at 60%

In the grey market, Deepa Jewellers shares were commanding a premium of Rs 44 on September 2, according to InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 177, the GMP implies an indicative listing price of Rs 221, translating into a potential listing gain of 24.86 percent.

Investors must note that the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and can change before the shares are listed.

Ahead of the public issue, Deepa Jewellers raised Rs 137.91 crore from 14 anchor investors. The company allotted 77.91 lakh shares to the anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

The anchor book included investors such as Nomura Singapore, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust Plc and Citigroup. Of the total anchor allocation, 14.96 lakh shares were allotted to domestic mutual funds, including Tata Asset Management Company and Unifi Mutual Fund.

Motilal Oswal Finvest was the largest investor in the anchor book, picking up 20.3 lakh shares worth Rs 35.95 crore. WhiteOak Capital and 360 ONE each acquired 5.08 lakh shares, with each investment amounting to nearly Rs 9 crore.

The company is looking to raise up to Rs 459.72 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 250 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 1.18 crore equity shares by promoter Ashish Agarwal and his wife Seema.

Check IPO News Here

Deepa Jewellers plans to deploy Rs 215 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards long-term working capital requirements, including procurement, maintenance and scaling up of inventory. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

The IPO has a lot size of 84 shares, requiring a minimum investment of Rs 14,868 for retail investors at the upper price band. The shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on September 8, subject to the IPO timeline.

Emkay Global Financial Services and Valmiki Leela Capital are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

2.headline: Rays of Belief IPO subscribed over 1.5x so far on Day 2; retail portion booked 8x
2.heading: Rays of Belief IPO subscribed over 1.5x so far on Day 2; retail portion booked 8x
2.intro: Rays of Belief, the parent company of Mom's Belief, continued to witness strong investor interest in its initial public offering (IPO) on the second day of bidding, with the issue recording nearly 1.5 times subscription, as of 10:20 am on September 2, as per the NSE data.
2.body:
Rays of Belief, the parent company of Mom's Belief, continued to witness strong investor interest in its initial public offering (IPO) on the second day of bidding, with the issue recording 1.5 times subscription, as of 10:20 am on September 2, as per the NSE data.

The Rs 125-crore IPO received bids for 46,58,308 equity shares against 31,37,810 shares on offer. Retail investors led the subscription, with their reserved portion subscribed 8.09 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 54 percent.

In the grey market, Rays of Belief shares were commanding a premium of Rs 38 on the morning of September 2, according to InvestorGain. Based on the upper price band of Rs 239, the grey market premium (GMP) indicates a potential listing gain of around 16 percent.

Read Also: Priority Jewels IPO allotment today: GMP signals 15% listing gain; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar

However, GMP is an unofficial indicator based on transactions in the unregulated grey market. The premium can change before listing and does not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.

Ahead of the IPO opening, Rays of Belief raised Rs 50 crore from five institutional investors through its anchor book. The anchor investors were allotted 20.92 lakh shares.

Viney Growth Fund and LRSD Securities were each allotted 6.27 lakh shares worth Rs 15 crore. Nova Global Opportunities Fund acquired 4.18 lakh shares worth Rs 10 crore.

Meanwhile, 31 Degrees North Fund and Visionary Value Fund were each allotted 2.09 lakh shares worth Rs 5 crore.

The company is looking to raise up to Rs 125 crore through the IPO, comprising 52.3 lakh shares. The price band has been fixed at Rs 227-239 per share, with the issue available for subscription from September 1 to September 3.

The IPO consists entirely of a fresh issue, with no offer-for-sale component.

Rays of Belief is promoted by Nitin Bindlish through Carving Futures. The company plans to deploy Rs 41.3 crore of the net IPO proceeds towards setting up new centres on leased premises and associated technology hardware costs.

Check IPO News Here

Another Rs 14.4 crore has been earmarked for lease payments for its existing centres in India, while Rs 10.1 crore will be invested in its subsidiary, Mom’s Belief US Inc, towards lease or licence payments for existing centres in the US.

The company will also use Rs 10.2 crore for brand awareness and inclusive outreach programmes. The remaining proceeds will be used to fund inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and for general corporate purposes.

Mefcom Capital Markets is the merchant banker for the IPO.
